summary: The registered universal_address_writer_equivariance preserves universal admission/post-state renaming over four source-shaped writer projections and adds LiveClaimBatchBehavior over arbitrary callee/context/request/hint/recipient/world inputs. Actual root success derives an ordered physical claim/CALL/event chain; root failure restores the entire modeled caller/callee world. The live execution limb has no supplied admission boolean or stage-success premise. Global caller/owner/callee-world renaming is not proved. Claim storage now enters and commits the executing account frame; its storage-stage effects preserve foreign-account words before the recipient callback. Under A-NO-REENTRY, PAddress1NoReentry derives that the claimed bit survives the recipient CALL. Live renaming (2026-09-19): PAddress1LiveRenaming.runClaimWithdrawalsTo_rename shows the registered live claim batch commutes with an abstract sender/owner renaming of the queue world for every equivariant recipient callee; actual_claim_batch_rename transports committed batches, their claim chains and the A-NO-REENTRY transcript.

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1.universal_address_writer_equivariance
theorems.doc:
/-- Two nonzero callers have the same source-shaped admission bit, and a
successful post-state renames under the swap.

Registered P-ADDRESS-1 parent. For two nonzero callers, the source-shaped
`run` admits `a₁` iff it admits `a₂` on the caller-swapped input, and a
successful post-state renames under the same swap. The claim is unconditional
over four modeled address-bearing writer projections: since wave 5,
`addressEquivarianceEntryScope` covers `claimWithdrawalsTo` too -- its
request-owner gate (`caller = requestOwner`) is caller-relative and renames
with the caller (`requestOwner` is an address-indexed input field renamed by
`renameInput`) -- so the scope is total over the modeled writers
(`addressEquivarianceEntryScope_total`). The wave-4 scope premise thereby
became vacuous: the source lemmas below hold for every `EntryPoint` via
`run_rename`, so the premise's deletion cannot break the proof, and per the
wave-4 load-bearing criterion it is no longer carried. On
`requestWithdrawals` and `unwrap`, admission is pause plus the caller's own
balance/allowance flags only (`pause_balance_admitted_is_permissionless`); it
does not test `caller = owner` or `caller = <fixed constant>`. Adding a
fixed-owner gate to that admission breaks equivariance via
`LidoSRv3.Tests.AddressSourceMutants.fixed_owner_gate_kill_line_refutes_parent`,
which negates this theorem's exact predicate shape on a mutant of this file's
own `admitted`/`run`/`renameInput` (not an unrelated toy entrypoint).

`wellFormedAddressInput` and `singletonActorEntryPoint` are deliberately not
carried as hypotheses here: neither restricts this conclusion (the proof
below needs only `a₁, a₂ ≠ 0`), and `singletonActorEntryPoint` is provably
`False` for every `EntryPoint` in this model
(`not_singleton_actor_entry_point`), so requiring its negation would add no
content while reading as a real exclusion. Carrying either as an unused
binder would hide that they are premise-free rather than making the claim
more honest. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem universal_address_writer_equivariance
    (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address) (h₁ : a₁ ≠ 0) (h₂ : a₂ ≠ 0)
    (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input) :
    (AdmissionIsCallerBlind a₁ a₂ inp ∧ PostStateRenamesWithCaller a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
      LiveClaimBatchBehavior

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1.abstract_source_verity_tx_address_equivariance
theorems.doc:
/-- Two nonzero callers have the same source-shaped admission bit, and a
successful post-state renames under the swap. Verity composition adds
`Contract.run` observe = `sourceAddressView` when the amount fits one word
and the balance/allowance flags are coherent, snapshot rollback on revert, and
the renamed run observing the renamed view.

Composition of (i) the universal source-shaped swap, (ii) each
`Contract.run` entrypoint's address-write `observe` matching
`sourceAddressView` when `amount < 2^256` and the balance/allowance
flags are coherent, (iii) any `Contract.run` revert restoring the
snapshot, (iv) the renamed input's TX view matching `postAddressView`
of the renamed post-state. Not a WQ claim. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem abstract_source_verity_tx_address_equivariance :
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      AdmissionIsCallerBlind a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      PostStateRenamesWithCaller a₁ a₂ inp) ∧
    (∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input),
      AmountFitsWord inp → BalanceFlagCoherent inp → AllowanceFlagCoherent inp →
      ObservesSourceView inp) ∧
    RevertRestoresSnapshot ∧
    (∀ (a₁ a₂ : Verity.Address), a₁ ≠ 0 → a₂ ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (inp : LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.Input) (post : PostState),
      LidoSRv3.Audit.SolidityAddress.run inp = .committed post →
      AmountFitsWord inp → BalanceFlagCoherent inp → AllowanceFlagCoherent inp →
      RenamedRunObservesRenamedView a₁ a₂ inp post)

assumptions.risk: The external callees reached by the modeled Lido, StakingRouter and gateway executions -- module obtainDepositData bodies, the beacon deposit contract, the EIP-7251 consolidation-request predeploy, the WithdrawalQueue finalization callback and the configured refund recipient -- do not call back into Lido, the router or the gateway. `LidoSRv3/Audit/Source/NoReentry.lean` names this on the Live external-call interpreter as `NoReentry (external : External) (self : List Address)`: a call targeting a protected address is rejected, an accepted reply returns a world agreeing with the received world on every protected address (all storage words and the balance), and no recorded nested attempt into a protected address was accepted. A callee that re-enters (for example a malicious module implementation or a refund recipient that calls back into the gateway) is not covered.
assumptions.justification: Thomas 2026-09-17 (step 1b of the "not proven" cleanup): the deployed callees are audited protocol contracts, the beacon deposit contract and an EIP predeploy, so their non-re-entry may be assumed rather than proved per body. The registry prose at `audit/topup-call-history/README.md:51` argued that adding a `noReentry` premise would not close the TOPUP-2 per-block cap; the owner overrides that reading for the five rows below, where the premise constrains only the callee interpreter of theorems that already thread the exact returned world, and where the corollaries are stated on those theorems. Corollaries: `PDeposit1NoReentry.actual_physical_metadata_conserves_no_reentry` (DEPOSIT-1 ledger plus `Confined other [lido, router]`), `PTopup1NoReentry.actual_continuation_locator_conserves_no_reentry` (TOPUP-1), `PReserve1NoReentry.actual_reserve_history_final_reserve` (RESERVE-1: the final reserve word equals the spending stage's), `PConsolidationEth1NoReentry.settlement_preserves_gateway_and_vault_storage` (ETH-1: gateway and vault storage equal the post-quota storage after the inbox and refund CALLs) and `PAddress1NoReentry.claim_returns_committed_storage` / `actual_claim_batch_no_reentry` (ADDRESS-1: the claimed bit and locked-ether write survive the recipient CALL; no accepted nested call into the queue). The generic consequences for `Live.call` are `call_storage`, `call_balance`, `call_self_rejected` and `call_nested_rejects`.
assumptions.violation_impact: If a callee re-enters Lido, the router or the gateway, the corollaries above do not apply: the final reserve, the gateway/vault storage after settlement, the claimed bit after a recipient CALL and the confinement of module/beacon calls are no longer derived, and the exact-returned-world parents must be consulted with the re-entrant world.
assumptions.validation: `lake build LidoSRv3.Audit.Source.NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PTopup1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PReserve1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PConsolidationEth1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1NoReentry` checks the corollaries. The premise itself is validated only by review of the pinned callee sources (NodeOperatorsRegistry/CSM obtainDepositData, deposit_contract.sol, the EIP-7251 predeploy, WithdrawalQueue.finalize, the refund recipient configuration); it is not proved for the deployed runtimes.
assumptions.removal_path: Prove `NoReentry` for each deployed callee body: model obtainDepositData of NOR/CSM, the beacon deposit contract, the EIP-7251 predeploy and WithdrawalQueue.finalize as Live executables and show they issue no CALL into Lido, the router or the gateway; bind the refund recipient configuration. Then replace the premise by those theorems in the five corollaries.

covered: Original universal source-shaped admission/post-state equivariance over transferFrom, requestWithdrawals, claimWithdrawalsTo and unwrap, without adding singleton-actor entrypoints; permissionless pause/balance/allowance admission is established only for requestWithdrawals and unwrap.

Registered LiveClaimBatchBehavior cases on runClaimWithdrawalsTo actual root outcome over arbitrary worlds and request/hint lists. Successful execution derives recipient and length guards and ClaimChain; failed execution restores the complete input world.

Each ClaimChain step derives packed owner/claimed/finalized checks, actual physical keccak queue/checkpoint/EnumerableSet reads and checked writes, source-computed payout and locked-ETH subtraction, funded recipient/value/empty-calldata CALL, callback-returned world/data/nested attempts, and ordered WithdrawalClaimed then Transfer events.

PayoutEffect exposes the provisional sender debit/recipient credit and either EOA success or the precise external-callee returned world. Later claims use that returned world, so earlier callback effects participate in whole-batch rollback.

Projection guard order follows the relevant source order: finalized before claimed/owner and owner before hint for claims; stETH allowance before balance for request transferFrom. The physical claim already checks recipient before array length and marks/removes the owned request before hint/payout calculation.

Parent-shaped admission and owner-write mutants retain the strengthened live conjunct while falsifying the source renaming conjunct. PackDAddressClaimMutants exercises actual CALL order/target, zero-recipient rejection, and root rollback.
Four source-shaped storage-writing Contract.run entrypoints retain their existing address-write observable correspondences; these remain separate from the actual callee-world execution plane.

PAddress1NoReentry (2026-09-17, A-NO-REENTRY): claim_returns_committed_storage derives from ClaimEffect that, under NoReentry callee [queue], the world after the recipient CALL holds exactly the claim's committed dirty storage (claimed bit and locked-ether write final) and the queue balance is the provisional payout transfer; actual_claim_batch_no_reentry is the registered-parent corollary (runClaimWithdrawalsTo_success) adding that no accepted nested attempt in the batch transcript targets the queue. The premise is assumed, not proved for the recipient.

live renaming of the claim batch (2026-09-19): PAddress1LiveRenaming.runClaimWithdrawalsTo_rename proves that renaming two addresses in the sender (renameContext) and in the request owners commutes with the registered live executor AddressRecipientCallBridge.runClaimWithdrawalsTo: for every LiveRenaming a1 a2 ctx (state: ContractState -> ContractState renaming the owner field of every request metadata word by renameOwnerWord and moving the owner-indexed length/value/index cells of o to renameAddress a1 a2 o, with the finalized id, checkpoint index, locked ether, amounts and checkpoint channels unchanged and the matching write commutations; world: World -> World with enter/commit commutation, balances and codeSize fixed, transfer commutation and the queue's WithdrawalClaimed/Transfer sender words renamed) and every callee with callee req (R.world w) = mapReply R.world (callee req w), runClaimWithdrawalsTo callee (renameContext a1 a2 ctx) ids hints recipient (R.world w) = mapResult R.world (runClaimWithdrawalsTo callee ctx ids hints recipient w). The renaming is abstract because the queue's channels live at computable keccak slots (mappingSlotLocation) with no injectivity in the model; a LiveRenaming exists exactly when the owner-bearing slot families do not collide with the other claim channels. The callee equivariance hypothesis is an explicit weakening: a recipient whose reply depends on the queue's owner words or on the sender identity is outside the result. actual_claim_batch_rename: a committed batch stays committed under the renaming with the renamed final world, the same attempts, the transported ClaimChain and, under NoReentry callee [ctx.self], no accepted nested call into the queue. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

Remaining: the renaming is abstract because keccak slot families (mappingSlotLocation) carry no injectivity in the model, so its existence is the collision-freedom of the owner-bearing slots; the recipient callee's equivariance is a hypothesis, not derived from A-NO-REENTRY; balances are not renamed; the other live writer bodies are not covered (see the next entries).
